title: Build content pipeline MVP
description: Implement the full guides/ content ingestion pipeline: project skeleton, LLM clients, queue/storage, fetchers, processors, tags, verify, orchestrator, stream/cron entrypoint. See docs/plans/2026-05-11-guides-mvp-implementation.md

title: Task 1: Project skeleton
description: pyproject.toml, .env.example, guides/__init__.py, guides/settings.py. Azure env + data paths + prompt dir. Verify: uv run python -c 'from guides.settings import Settings; print(ok)'

title: queue: mixed classification — extract only standalone-line URLs, not inline
description: In guides/queue.py _extract_urls() currently grabs every URL in text including inline references (e.g. RFC links in prose). Fix: in _classify_text_file and scan_inbox, only consider a URL as 'extractable' if it appears on its own line or as a markdown list item (line matches r'^\s*[-*]?\s*https?://' or line.strip().startswith('http')). This prevents creating noise articles from inline citation URLs. Files: guides/queue.py

title: quality_score: compute and write to frontmatter after verify
description: In verify.py run_verify(), after running checks, compute quality_score = sum(checks.values()) / len(checks). Pass it back in the returned tuple. In run.py, receive it and pass to wrap_with_frontmatter as quality_score param. In process/wiki.py wrap_with_frontmatter(), accept quality_score: float | None = None and write 'quality_score: 0.78' instead of 'quality_score: null'. This unlocks needs-review filtering. Files: guides/verify.py, guides/run.py, guides/process/wiki.py

title: Untrack .env from git history (security)
description: Файл .env з API-ключами відслідковується git (незважаючи на .gitignore). Треба: 1) git rm --cached .env 2) перевірити чи є .env в попередніх комітах, якщо є — очистити через git filter-branch або BFG 3) переконатись що .gitignore справно ігнорує. Не ламати .env файл, лише прибрати з git tracking.

title: Prevent duplicate source pages for repeated local inputs
description: The same local source was ingested into two separate source bundles and two wiki pages with hash suffixes, even though it was a single test input. Investigate queue/inbox deduplication, source-dir creation, and wiki slug collision behavior so one source does not create duplicate outputs within the same batch unless explicitly intended as a split case.
acceptance_criteria: A single local input file yields one canonical source bundle and one wiki page in a normal run; accidental duplicate pages with slug hash suffixes are eliminated or explicitly explained by split logic.
notes: Observed a separate failure mode during rerun: all 9 items failed in sandbox with DNS/APIConnectionError to Azure, so duplicate prevention could not be evaluated on that run. Preparing an unrestricted rerun to validate the lock under real connectivity.

title: Sync review status between meta.json and wiki frontmatter
description: Current pipeline writes source bundle meta.json with status=needs_review for generated outputs, but wiki pages keep frontmatter status=active, review_required=false, verified=false. This makes manual review unreliable because the human-facing wiki layer hides the review state. Align the wiki frontmatter and indexes with the pipeline verification result so pages that need review are visibly marked in the wiki.
acceptance_criteria: When verify returns needs_review, the corresponding wiki page frontmatter reflects that state (status and/or review_required), and review indexes/logs show it consistently with data/sources/*/meta.json.
notes: Observed sandbox-only network failure to Azure during rerun; frontmatter sync changes are implemented and unit-tested, but require a successful unrestricted batch to validate on generated outputs.

title: Fix title and slug extraction for local markdown sources
description: Local markdown sources can generate placeholder titles like 'Title', producing bad wiki slugs such as title.md even when the document has a real semantic heading or filename. Improve title extraction for local files so placeholder headings are ignored and wiki page titles/slugs fall back to the real document title or source filename intelligently.
acceptance_criteria: A source like PRD/current/07-prompts.md no longer produces title.md. The resulting wiki page gets a meaningful title and slug derived from real content or a sane file-based fallback.
notes: Added regression test for placeholder '# Title' headings in local markdown and updated title inference to skip placeholder headings and use the next meaningful line.

title: P1: Prevent duplicate processing in concurrent pipeline runs
P1: Sync verify status to wiki frontmatter (review_required)
Pre-run cleanup: clear inbox.txt, old wiki pages, wiki/log.md
description: Clear data/queue/inbox.txt (old t.me URL), remove old wiki/extracts pages (articles/3-claude-code.md, githubs/llm*.md), clear wiki/log.md. Leaves data/inbox/ with 9 clean corpus files ready for first pipeline run.

title: Prepare guides for first clean smoke run
description: Make the guides workspace test-ready for the first clean smoke run. Remove stale queue/wiki artifacts, keep only curated inbox sources, and fix any immediate runtime blockers that would make the first result misleading or broken.
acceptance_criteria: Running the local entrypoint processes only the curated inbox seed set, old wiki/output noise is gone, and the first smoke run can produce understandable results in data/sources and wiki/extracts.
notes: Cleaned generated output layer for a real first smoke run: data/queue/inbox.txt is empty; data/inbox now contains the 9 test source files; data/sources was reset; wiki/extracts was reset to empty type folders with .gitkeep only; wiki/log.md was reset; queue/needs_review was reset; pipeline.log was removed. Remaining caveat: I have not executed the full LLM-backed run from sandbox because outbound model/network calls are restricted here, but the workspace is now clean for the user's local run.

title: Run end-to-end pipeline test with corpus inbox files

Check: 1) Any import errors 2) Which files were processed vs quarantined 3) What was written to wiki/extracts/ 4) Check wiki/log.md for entries 5) Report any errors from data/logs/pipeline.log. Command: uv run python process_stream.py 2>&1. Do NOT fix pipeline bugs found - just report them clearly.

title: Run import smoke test: verify pipeline imports and queue detection
description: Verify the pipeline is importable and queue detection works without LLM calls. Run: uv run python -c 'from guides.run import run_pipeline; from guides.queue import pop_pending, scan_inbox; from guides.vault import store; from guides.tracing import init_tracing; print("imports ok")'. Also verify detect_source_type() works for 5 sample inputs: https://github.com/simonw/llm, https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=abc, https://t.me/channel/123, https://example.com/article, /path/to/file.pdf. Report any import errors or detection failures.

acceptance_criteria: A shortlist of 2-3 ALF candidate sources is documented with original paths, source type, why each is useful for testing fetch/process/wiki quality, and any risk notes.
notes: Done: selected and copied 2 ALF sources into data/inbox with manifest at data/inbox/MANIFEST.md. Files: 05-alf-implementing-claude-code-skills-from-scratch.md, 06-alf-context-engineering-for-agents.md.

title: Curate LAAI reference corpus shortlist for guides testing
description: Select 3-4 high-signal local source texts from /Users/khabaroff/DEV/LAAI for guides pipeline smoke tests. Focus on source quality, prompt relevance, wiki/extract fit, and technical learning value. Do not copy files yet; produce only the approved candidate list and rationale.
acceptance_criteria: A shortlist of 3-4 LAAI candidate sources is documented with original paths, source type, why each is useful for testing fetch/process/wiki quality, and any risk notes.
notes: Done: selected and copied 4 LAAI sources into data/inbox with manifest at data/inbox/MANIFEST.md. Files: 01-laai-building-effective-ai-agents.txt, 02-laai-demystifying-evals-for-ai-agents.txt, 03-laai-curated-context-engineering-vs-llm-wiki.txt, 04-laai-prd-prompts.md.

title: Prepare guides workspace for clean test run
description: Clean stale generated artifacts, old logs, and transient outputs from the guides workspace so the next test run starts from a predictable baseline. Preserve planning and documentation files; remove only generated/runtime data that should not survive into a clean test.
acceptance_criteria: old generated logs and transient runtime outputs are removed; docs and plans remain intact; workspace is ready for a clean test run from an empty or predictable baseline.

title: Add local cost report command for guides usage logs
description: Port the useful reporting pattern from ALF's src/cost_report.py into guides. The project already plans local usage logging; now it needs an operator-facing report command that reads usage.db and/or JSONL cost logs and shows spending by run, by model, and over time. This is for practical visibility, not observability theatre.
acceptance_criteria: guides has a simple cost report command or script; it can show totals by run and by model; it can filter by recent period; it reads local logs as the source of truth; the output is usable for everyday manual inspection.

title: Add provider-agnostic token and cost accounting helper
description: Borrow the useful accounting approach from ALF and LAAI: create one small helper layer that normalizes usage extraction, estimates token counts when provider usage is missing, and calculates best-effort cost from model metadata. This helper should feed usage.db and JSONL logs without forcing every processor or adapter to reimplement accounting logic.
acceptance_criteria: a shared helper extracts usage from Azure/OpenAI-style and other compatible responses; missing usage falls back to best-effort estimation; cost calculation is centralized; pipeline logging consumes this helper instead of duplicating token/cost logic in multiple places.

title: Add pipeline logging and token-cost usage tracking
description: Implement the observability layer from docs/wiki-v1-plan.md. Write stage logs to data/logs/*.jsonl and usage/cost rows to data/state/usage.db. Track run_id, item_id, stage, source_type, status, fallback_used, duration_ms, error data, model, prompt_version, tokens_in, tokens_out, and cost_usd. Local logs are the source of truth; external tooling like Langfuse can remain optional later.
acceptance_criteria: pipeline writes events/fetch/process/errors JSONL logs; usage.db contains a usable usage_log table; each LLM stage records token and cost data when available and best-effort estimates when not; fallback use and failures are visible for later analysis.

title: Adapt prompt set to Wiki V1 extract-page contract
description: Revise the current prompt files so they target the actual Wiki V1 output shape instead of a generic summary. Prompts must produce dense Russian extract-pages for the primary reader, preserve English technical terms where useful, emit the required frontmatter/body contract, and support controlled metadata fields such as knowledge_kinds, topics, entities, and concepts. This includes article, youtube, github/reference, tags/metadata, and verify prompts.
acceptance_criteria: prompt files align with docs/wiki-v1-plan.md, docs/wiki-schema-for-guides.md, docs/frontmatter-examples.md, and docs/body-templates.md; output target is a dense Russian extract-page for the user; generic summary wording is removed where it conflicts with the wiki contract.

title: Implement Wiki V1 filesystem layout
description: Adopt docs/wiki-v1-plan.md as the canonical wiki layout. The pipeline must treat data/ as the technical/raw layer and wiki/ as the human-facing layer. Create and use: wiki/extracts/{articles,youtubes,pdfs,githubs,notes}/, wiki/_indexes/, and wiki/log.md. Raw source content stays only in data/sources/.
acceptance_criteria: wiki/ contains extracts/, _indexes/, and log.md; data/sources/ remains raw-only; no raw source.md files are copied into wiki; layout matches docs/wiki-v1-plan.md exactly.

title: Implement controlled wiki metadata schema for extract pages
description: Enforce the metadata model from docs/wiki-v1-plan.md and docs/wiki-schema-for-guides.md. Replace the idea of one loose tags array with controlled fields: source_type, knowledge_kinds, topics, entities, concepts, plus review/verification/provenance fields. The goal is a stable schema that supports later concept/entity extraction without needing concept pages in v1.
acceptance_criteria: extract pages include source_type, knowledge_kinds, topics, entities, concepts, status, review_required, verified, quality_score, source_paths, prompt_version, and provenance; source_type and knowledge_kinds use controlled lists; no raw semantic meaning is encoded in folder layout beyond source type.

title: Route extract pages by source type into wiki/extracts
description: Write processed pages into wiki/extracts by source type instead of keeping final pages inside data/sources/. Use these target folders only: articles, youtubes, pdfs, githubs, notes. File names are slug-based; on collision add a short hash suffix. Default rule is one source -> one extract-page, with split support only as an explicit special case for very long YouTube or PDF sources.
acceptance_criteria: article outputs land in wiki/extracts/articles/; youtube in youtubes/; pdf in pdfs/; github repo/tool/skill links in githubs/; local notes in notes/; slug naming works; collisions get deterministic short suffixes; raw source path is preserved in frontmatter.

title: Generate wiki indexes and human-readable wiki log
description: Implement automatic markdown index generation for wiki/_indexes/ and append-only wiki/log.md after each successful run. Initial indexes required by docs/wiki-v1-plan.md: recent.md, by-topic.md, by-kind.md, needs-review.md, githubs.md, prompts.md. wiki/log.md should stay short and human-readable: ingests, fallback use, verify failures, and page writes, but no stack traces or token spam.
acceptance_criteria: all six index pages are generated or refreshed automatically; wiki/log.md is appended with concise event lines; needs-review and prompt/github views are navigable by eye; indexes are derived from extract page frontmatter, not handwritten.

title: Manual review: validate prompts against real study sources
description: Run a manual review of the prompt set with the project owner after the prompts are adapted. Use 5-6 real source cases from the intended workflow: article, long article, youtube transcript, github repo, pdf, and note. Review whether the resulting extract-pages feel like dense personal working notes, whether prompts preserve code/commands/prompts, whether Russian remains the main wiki language, and whether metadata feels useful for visual browsing. This task is intentionally human-in-the-loop.
acceptance_criteria: owner reviews at least 5 real outputs; reviewer marks what feels too fluffy, too lossy, or wrongly structured; decisions are written down as prompt adjustments or follow-up issues; prompt set is explicitly approved for v1 or sent back for revision.

title: Add schema-aware verify coverage for frontmatter and body templates
description: Implement verification coverage specifically for the wiki-ready output contract. verify.py must check not only file existence and non-empty output, but also required frontmatter fields, valid page type/source type combinations, presence of tags/topics/entities/concepts, and required body sections from docs/body-templates.md. This issue is distinct from processor adoption: it enforces the contract after generation.
acceptance_criteria: verify checks required frontmatter keys from docs/wiki-schema-for-guides.md; verify checks body sections for article.md and reference.md based on docs/body-templates.md; verify can fail outputs with missing schema fields or malformed body shape; tests or fixtures cover at least article, youtube, github_repo, and noisy PDF cases.

title: Adopt wiki schema in processors and verify
description: Implement the wiki-ready page contract from docs/wiki-schema-for-guides.md across processors and verification. article.py, youtube.py, and reference.py must emit frontmatter and body structure that match the schema. verify.py must validate required frontmatter fields, page type/source type consistency, and the presence of tags/topics/entities/concepts/provenance/source_paths. This issue makes the wiki schema an enforced MVP behavior instead of documentation only.
acceptance_criteria: article and youtube outputs are valid source-page documents; github output is a valid reference-page document; processors emit required frontmatter fields; body follows documented section templates; verify rejects missing or malformed schema fields; end-to-end output matches docs/wiki-schema-for-guides.md and docs/frontmatter-examples.md.

title: Task 4: Source detection + shared models

title: script: reprocess pages with placeholder '# Title' in body
description: Write scripts/reprocess_stale.py: 1) scan all wiki/extracts/**/*.md, 2) find pages where body (after frontmatter) starts with '# Title', 3) for each: look up source path from source_paths or sources/ meta.json, 4) delete the source dir in data/sources/, 5) if source is a file — copy to data/inbox/ for reprocessing; if URL — add to data/queue/inbox.txt. Then run process_stream.py. Currently affected: notes/07-prompts.md, notes/formal-schema-for-verified-multi-model-knowledge.md — both processed before prompt fix.

title: indexes: populate needs-review.md from quality_score < 0.7

If quality_score is not null and < 0.7 (or status == 'needs_review'), add entry to _indexes/needs-review.md. Currently the index is always empty. Depends on guides-kfd (quality_score computation). Format: same as recent.md — '## DATE | [[slug]] - title (type) quality_score: X.XX'. Files: guides/enrich/indexes.py

Also update prompts/tags_extract.md to say 'entities: named entities ≤5 самых значимых' and 'concepts: ≤4 абстрактных концепции'. Tags prompt already says 3-8, so tags are OK. Goal: reduce entity noise (e.g. ANTHROPIC_API_KEY appearing as entity). Files: guides/enrich/tags.py, guides/prompts/tags_extract.md

Напиши короткий звіт: OK або що треба фіксити.

title: Normalize wiki frontmatter for local file sources
description: Wiki pages generated from local files currently carry misleading frontmatter values such as origin=url, url=<local path>, language=en for Russian-written extracts, empty source_paths, and zeroed provenance. Normalize frontmatter semantics for file-based sources so downstream agents can trust the metadata layer.
acceptance_criteria: For local file inputs, frontmatter uses correct origin/source path fields, avoids storing local paths in url, sets language according to the wiki output policy, and populates source_paths/provenance fields according to the current schema contract.
notes: Current pass keeps local-file frontmatter normalized for origin=file, url='', language=ru, and source_paths populated. Full semantic normalization still to be validated on rerun outputs.

title: Fix slug fallback in vault._extract_title when title is placeholder
Fix frontmatter metadata: origin/url/language for FILE sources

acceptance_criteria: A curated seed set of local markdown sources is copied into data/inbox/; a manifest file records original paths and rationale; only high-signal items relevant to the guides system are included.
notes: Done: seeded data/inbox with 6 curated local sources from LAAI and ALF. Manifest documents original paths and rationale.

title: Add optional Langfuse tracing on top of local logs
description: Guides should keep local JSONL and usage.db as the source of truth, but add optional external tracing for easier inspection. Following the ALF pattern, integrate Langfuse as a feature-flagged observability layer for prompt/model traces, linked to run_id and item_id. The integration must be optional and must never block the pipeline if Langfuse is unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: Langfuse can be enabled by config/env; traces include run_id and item_id correlation; failures in Langfuse do not break the pipeline; local logs remain authoritative even when Langfuse is enabled.

title: Add safe handling for malformed or unknown ingestion inputs
description: Harden ingestion against empty files, broken URLs, unknown binary files, and other malformed inputs. The pipeline must skip or quarantine bad inputs, log why they were rejected, and continue processing the rest of the batch. Based on docs/ingestion-cases.md case 10.
acceptance_criteria: Malformed inputs never abort the full ingestion run; each rejected input produces a clear reason in logs or meta; unsupported inputs become needs_review or are safely skipped by policy; tests cover empty, broken, and unknown inputs.

title: Add URL extraction from text and markdown files
description: Implement ingestion heuristics for .txt and .md files in data/inbox/. The system must distinguish between a file that is only a link container and a file that is a real standalone source. Support: single-link files, files that are mainly lists of links, and mixed text-with-links cases. Base this on docs/ingestion-cases.md cases 3, 4, 5, and 6.
acceptance_criteria: Single-link file becomes one URL QueueItem; link-list file expands into multiple URL QueueItems; mixed-content note can remain a standalone file source; heuristics are explicit in code and covered by tests; origin/meta preserves that input came from a file.

title: Add PDF ingestion and extraction failure handling
description: Support PDF files placed into data/inbox/. Detect PDF input, route it into a text extraction path, and continue into ARTICLE processing when extraction succeeds. If extraction fails or yields unusable text, mark the source as needs_review instead of failing the whole run. Based on docs/ingestion-cases.md case 7.
acceptance_criteria: PDF files are detected; extracted text is passed downstream as ARTICLE input; extraction failures are recorded as needs_review; one passing and one failing PDF case are covered by tests or fixtures.

title: Add robust inbox.txt ingestion
description: Implement ingestion for data/queue/inbox.txt as a stable queue input. Support one entity per line, trimming whitespace, skipping empty lines, deduplicating within a single run, and tolerating malformed lines without aborting the whole pass. This covers the MVP cases for one URL and multiple URLs in inbox.txt from docs/ingestion-cases.md.
acceptance_criteria: Reads one URL or file path per line; ignores empty lines; deduplicates duplicate lines within one run; malformed lines do not abort the batch; emits QueueItem objects for valid lines.

Each reads its prompt .md. Verify: fixture input → markdown output with title.

title: Accept Telegram links as ingestion inputs

Fetching may still end in needs_review if raw content cannot yet be extracted. Preserve metadata that the source was a Telegram link. Based on docs/ingestion-cases.md case 8.
acceptance_criteria: t.me URLs pass ingestion validation; QueueItem/meta can mark them as telegram_link; Telegram URLs do not crash the pipeline; unsupported fetch path degrades to needs_review rather than silent drop.

title: Build ingestion fixture matrix and manual smoke cases
description: Create a reusable set of real-world ingestion fixtures and manual smoke cases covering: single URL, multiple URLs, link-list markdown, mixed text plus link, standalone markdown/text, YouTube URL, GitHub repo URL, Telegram URL, and PDF. This is the practical validation layer for docs/ingestion-cases.md and should be runnable by developers before calling ingestion done.
acceptance_criteria: Fixture set exists for the core ingestion cases; developers can run a documented smoke pass; expected outcomes are defined per case; failures are easy to inspect in source/output storage.

title: Task 9: Orchestrator
description: guides/run.py: wire detect → fetch → process → tag → verify → store. Status handling: success/failed/needs_review. Verify: end-to-end on 3 samples (article URL, YouTube URL, GitHub repo URL), output folders in data/sources/.
